newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares down despite heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares down despite heavy trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices continued to slip on Sunday with many popular stocks closing at lower prices despite active trade.
The all-share index fell 5.82 points to 392.72, its lowest level since February 3. It was the fourth consecutive slip for the index which climaxed on February 24 at 427.77 points.
Brokers have said profit taking and a natural correction are the reasons for the slip.
Volume on Sunday was a high 103.39 million pounds ($30.45 million), the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said in its daily report.
Commerical International Bank was Sunday's most active share, trading in more than 17.60 million pounds but it lost 43.8 pounds to close at 831.66, the CMAsaid.
General Silos and Storage was the second most active share, with more than 13.80 million pounds changing hands but it closed 5.49 pounds lower at 105.62.
Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA was one of the few active shares that closed higher, rising 2.35 pounds to end trading at 80.00 pounds after more than 10 million pounds changed hands.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills WCFM.CA traded in more than 9.40 million pounds but it slipped 2.62 to close at 111.5.
Walid el-Khouli, from Rashad Securities Brokerage, said the milling sector was beginning to pick up from a recent slump.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 637.16 points from 685.53 points on Thursday but the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose, closing at 263.62 from 263.47.
Out of the 91 shares traded, 26 gained, 37 lost and 28 ended the day unchanged.
